SPACES.label: Problem
SPACES.blurb: Who, in what context, with what problems, wanting what outcomes.

SPACES.label: Bets
SPACES.blurb: The bets we are making and what we assume; how we will know. Not necessarily scientific hypotheses.

SPACES.label: Solution
SPACES.blurb: Capabilities, features (one per would-be department), agents, journeys, domain, architecture, screens.

SPACES.label: Current state
SPACES.blurb: Code and references into the repository, infrastructure, practices and protocols, and the current test results.

SPACES.label: Planned changes
SPACES.blurb: Epics and the super-targeted coding-agent tasks under them, each naming the tests it must turn green.

SPACES.label: Effects
SPACES.blurb: Metric readings, usage events, user feedback, evidence: what confirms or denies the bets.

KINDS.label: Name
KINDS.blurb: What the system is called.

KINDS.label: Purpose
KINDS.blurb: Why it exists; the real-world effect and value it is for.

KINDS.label: Summary
KINDS.blurb: A paragraph for picking this project out of a list.

KINDS.label: Audience
KINDS.blurb: A type of person or agent the system is for.

KINDS.label: Context
KINDS.blurb: The situation an audience is in when the problem shows up.

KINDS.label: Use case
KINDS.blurb: Something an audience is trying to get done.

KINDS.label: Problem
KINDS.blurb: What stands in their way today.

KINDS.label: Outcome
KINDS.blurb: The change we want for the audience. Should be measurable.

KINDS.label: Bet

needs.ask: How would you know "{title}" holds? Name one metric.

KINDS.blurb: A bet linking what we build to an outcome; some are specific and testable, some are just bets.

KINDS.label: Assumption
KINDS.blurb: Taken as true until reality says otherwise.

KINDS.label: Goal
KINDS.blurb: An outcome we want, stated as a compound of metrics; for the audience or for ourselves as the business.

KINDS.label: Metric
KINDS.blurb: How an outcome or hypothesis will be measured.

KINDS.label: Capability
KINDS.blurb: A high-level thing the system can do.

KINDS.label: Feature
KINDS.blurb: A value grouping, described by journeys and flows. What a startup would have a department for becomes a feature here.

KINDS.label: Flow
KINDS.blurb: A happy path through the system; touches architecture via uses edges. Corresponds across Overview and the architecture diagrams — selecting one dims everything else, everywhere.

KINDS.label: Term
KINDS.blurb: A fixed word of the domain.

KINDS.label: System
KINDS.blurb: The system itself as one bubble, or a meaningfully separate part of it (web vs mobile).

KINDS.label: External system
KINDS.blurb: Another system ours talks to.

KINDS.label: Module

needs.ask: What does "{title}" expose to the rest of the system? Name its interface.

KINDS.blurb: A business domain / bounded context. Always exposes an interface.

KINDS.label: Infra
KINDS.blurb: A deployable: dedicated infrastructure (cache, durable object, client, server, store, queue). Shown inside its module (contains) and, at the deployment level, by its role.

KINDS.label: Thing
KINDS.blurb: An entity in domain language; a noun.

KINDS.label: Rule

needs.ask: How would we know "{title}" holds? One test per line, naming the condition.

KINDS.blurb: Logic about one or more things, from hasMany to expectations. Should be tested both ways.

KINDS.label: Interface
KINDS.blurb: The API a module exposes; REST, RPC, UI or events. Molecules — payloads — enter as `in` and leave as `out`, through a `carries` edge to the things they are or derive from.

KINDS.label: Event
KINDS.blurb: Something notable that happened; a past-tense fact in the vocabulary.

KINDS.label: Protocol

needs.ask: What practice realises "{title}" today, or is this a planned change?

KINDS.blurb: How we want to enact the representation: PR gates, regular security audits, changelogs as blog posts. Reality's practices realise them. The product automation zone.

KINDS.label: Test

fields.label: Condition (one line of the rule it verifies)

KINDS.blurb: The bridge to reality: one per condition in a rule. Ladder: module exists (health check) → API surface → deterministic simulation. One kind of test; `resultSource` varies.

KINDS.label: Screen
KINDS.blurb: A user interface; composed of layouts and components.

KINDS.label: Design system
KINDS.blurb: Guides product and marketing material, including tone.

KINDS.label: Agent
KINDS.blurb: Executes actions for one or more features; a sub-item of the orchestration capability.

KINDS.label: AI function
KINDS.blurb: A named place the AI acts: its own prompt, declared context needs, output shape, a deterministic stub, and a feedback mechanism to measure efficacy.

KINDS.label: Repository
KINDS.blurb: Where the actual code lives; the thing codeRefs point into.

KINDS.label: Code
KINDS.blurb: A reference into the repository: a module, file or block as it actually exists.

KINDS.label: Infrastructure
KINDS.blurb: What is actually provisioned and running.

KINDS.label: Practice
KINDS.blurb: Best practices and protocols in force: process flows, CI, conventions.

KINDS.label: Asset
KINDS.blurb: A non-code artefact in force: landing page, pitch deck, price list, contract template, onboarding guide.

KINDS.label: Test result
KINDS.blurb: Whether a test is fulfilled in reality right now. Business-level tests report a metric value against a threshold; code tests report pass/fail.

KINDS.label: Epic
KINDS.blurb: A planned change, Jira-epic sized; exists only because some tests are not fulfilled.

KINDS.label: Task
KINDS.blurb: A super-targeted coding-agent task: names the tests it must turn green. Moves done → verified only once its suite is green and the reviewer agent's verdict says serves-intent; overfits or unclear sends it back to blocked.

KINDS.label: Metric reading
KINDS.blurb: A value of a metric at a time; business metrics as much as product ones.

KINDS.label: Usage event
KINDS.blurb: Something a user or customer did: a click, a signup, a lead captured, a deal closed, an invoice paid.

KINDS.label: Feedback
KINDS.blurb: What users and customers said, in their words.

KINDS.label: Evidence
KINDS.blurb: An observation from reality tied to a bet or metric.

EDGE_TYPES.label: motivates
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Is the reason the target exists (purpose → outcome, problem → outcome).

EDGE_TYPES.label: has
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Conceptual possession (audience has problem, use case has problem).

EDGE_TYPES.label: emits
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Produces an event (interface or rule emits event).

EDGE_TYPES.label: measures
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Metric reading measures a metric; usage events and feedback measure an outcome or feature.

EDGE_TYPES.label: targets
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Task or epic targets the tests it must turn green.

EDGE_TYPES.label: reports
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Test result reports on a test (reality → representation).

EDGE_TYPES.label: realises
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Actual code realises a solution-space module or item (current state → solution).

EDGE_TYPES.label: governs
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Rule governs a thing (or several: relationship rules).

EDGE_TYPES.label: verifies
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Test verifies a rule (one per condition).

EDGE_TYPES.label: carries
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Interface carries a payload that is or derives from this thing ("molecules" entering/leaving through the interface's in/out).

EDGE_TYPES.label: hosts
EDGE_TYPES.hint: Deployable (infra) hosts a module, at the deployment level. Additional to `contains` (module → infra), which the Modules grid still reads — do not repurpose that one.

RELATIONS.need: How would you know "{title}" holds? Name one metric.
